result.description: AARON MARINE OFFSHORE AUSTRALIA PTY. LTD.   ABOUT THE ROLE   AMO Australia is seeking an experienced Fire Protection Equipment Technician to conduct inspection, testing, service, maintenance, repair and recertification support for marine fire protection equipment and related safety systems onboard vessels, offshore installations, shipyards and at AMO workshop facilities.  The role is primarily focused on portable and fixed marine fire-fighting equipment and fire suppression systems. As AMO’s operations involve both fire-fighting equipment services and life-saving appliance services, the successful candidate will be required to support lifeboat, rescue boat, davit, winch and related LSA inspection, maintenance and testing activities in accordance with company procedures, manufacturer instructions, and applicable class, flag and customer requirements.  The successful candidate will work as part of a safety-critical service team and must operate strictly within documented competence, company approval, manufacturer authorisation where required, and applicable regulatory requirements. Honest defect reporting, correct system reinstatement and refusal to pass non-compliant equipment are non-negotiable requirements of the position.            Benefits   Task & responsibilities   General Duties    Carry out Maintenance, Overhaul, Repair and Test (MROT) work in accordance with approved procedures, OEM instructions, Class/Flag/customer requirements and company standards.  Prepare for each job by checking the job scope, procedure, risk assessment, permit requirements, tools, calibrate test equipment, spare parts, service kits and required documentation.  Conduct or participate in toolbox talks, risk assessments, isolation checks, permit-to-work controls and barricading before safety-critical work.  Use correct PPE and always follow vessel/site safety requirements.  Stop working immediately where a procedure, equipment condition, lifting arrangement, pressure system, release system, electrical/control system or work environment is unsafe.  Report defects honestly and clearly, even where there is customer pressure to pass equipment.  Do not bypass safety devices, defeat interlocks, shortcut functional tests or leave systems incorrectly reset.  Maintain tools, service kits, workshop equipment and company property in clean, safe and serviceable condition.    Primary Duties - Marine Fire Protection Equipment and Fixed Suppression Systems    Inspect, test, service, maintain, recharge/refill, pressure-test or arrange testing of portable and mobile fire extinguishers within company approval and technician competence.  Inspect and service fire hoses, nozzles, hydrants, international shore connections, fire blankets, fireman outfits, BA sets, BA cylinders, SCBA, EEBDs, medical oxygen equipment and associated compressed gas cylinders as applicable.  Check pressure, weight, seals, hoses, nozzles, cylinders, valves, gauges, hydrostatic test dates, expiry dates, brackets, labels, physical condition, accessibility and correct stowage/location.  Inspect, test, maintain and troubleshoot fixed fire-fighting and suppression systems including CO2 systems, foam systems, water mist systems, wet chemical systems, dry powder systems, helideck foam systems and related control/release arrangements, where within documented competence.  Inspect CO2 cylinders, cylinder banks, manifolds, flexible hoses, discharge piping, nozzles, release cabinets, pull cables, pilot cylinders, discharge heads, bursting discs, non-return valves and pressure-operated controls.  Check remote release stations, manual release controls, time-delay units, alarms, ventilation shutdowns, fuel shutdowns, fire dampers, lockable release arrangements, operating instructions and warning signage.  Carry out functional testing of alarms, release controls, shutdowns, pressure switches, flow switches, pumps, valves and control panels without accidental discharge and ensure systems are correctly reset and returned to operational condition.  Inspect and maintain BA compressors, air quality testing equipment and associated compressor/cylinder systems where trained and authorised.  Clearly tag and immediately report impaired, isolated, disconnected, expired, defective or unsafe fire protection equipment or systems to the vessel/client and AMO supervisor.       Secondary Duties - LSA, Lifeboat, Rescue Boat, Davit and Winch Support    Assist with inspection, service, maintenance, repair, testing and recertification support for lifeboats, rescue boats, davits, winches, launching appliances, release systems and associated deck safety equipment.  Support annual and five-year inspections, operational tests, load tests, winch/davit checks, launching/recovery checks and related documentation in accordance with SOLAS, MSC.402(96), class/flag/customer requirements and manufacturer instructions where applicable.
